A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BiSSL research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V4 reports original classification and object-detection experiments, MAE evaluations, ablations and dataset-size analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V5 reports original classification, detection and segmentation results, baseline comparisons, sensitivity experiments and backbone-alignment measurements.

M1.justification: The BiSSL objectives and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Limited adaptations appear: v5 Section C.6 trains a replacement projection head for checkpoints lacking one. Detection parameter handling also changes from assigning post-C4 layers to the pretext head in v4 Section B.6 to explicitly substituting corresponding conv5 parameters across levels in v5 Section B.7.

E1.justification: V5 adds semantic segmentation on VOC07+12 and Cityscapes, introducing pixel-level prediction and urban-scene coverage beyond v4's classification and detection evaluations. The existing classification datasets, ImageNet and STL10 remain represented.

E2.justification: V5 Table 3 adds randomly initialized backbones, linear probing, zero-initialized classification heads and continued pretraining on mixed pretext/downstream data as evaluated comparators. NoisyTune and the weighted-objective baseline already appeared in v4 Table 11; the IJ-discarded variant already appeared in v4 Table 8.

E3.justification: Selected post-BiSSL fine-tuning hyperparameters change substantially between v4 Table 5 and v5 Table 7, while the baseline and upper-level hyperparameter tables remain unchanged. V5 introduces segmentation protocols, parameter/feature similarity measurements and an official-checkpoint experiment using T=200, NU=4 and NL=10. These establish revised or additional reported settings, without establishing that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: V5 adds a regularization-weight sensitivity sweep, quantitative backbone-alignment analysis and an official-checkpoint/higher-resolution robustness evaluation. Existing upper-level iteration and IJ-discarding analyses are retained and extended to CUB200. Conversely, v4's Pets samples-per-class study and the top-5 pretraining-duration curve are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations from ten fine-tuning seeds. V5 Section B.6 newly specifies an exact two-sample permutation test over 184,756 assignments, its independence assumption and a p<0.01 threshold. V4 marked significant differences without documenting this procedure; no increase in run count is stated.

E6.justification: Many retained scores are replaced: Table 1's SimCLR/BiSSL CUB200 accuracy changes from 59.2±0.2 to 55.7±0.2, alongside revised fine-tuning hyperparameters. Table 2's SimCLR detection FT/BiSSL scores change from 59.6/60.6 to 53.1/54.4 under the revised adaptation. V5 adds segmentation, comparator, similarity and robustness results; BiSSL ranks first on four of five datasets in Table 3. SimCLR BiSSL computation time changes from 68 to 83 GPU hours. V5 Table 11 also reports an inconsistent BYOL/Food difference of +1.3 despite scores of 91.9 and 92.3.

T1.justification: V4 Appendix A.1's Theorem 1 and proof concerning omission of the second upper-level term are deleted. The retained implicit-Jacobian derivation gains explicit strong-convexity and twice-differentiable/L-smooth assumptions in v5 Appendix A.1, with qualifications about their practical validity. V5 also introduces similarity definitions in Equations (11)–(13); Equation (11) incorrectly uses squared L2 norms to normalize cosine similarity.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a task-agnostic intermediate bilevel stage that improves downstream alignment and fine-tuning. V5 broadens the abstract's empirical scope and explicitly adds semantic-segmentation improvements and consistency across experimental settings in the introduction. The principal methodological and alignment claims retain their meaning.

C2.justification: V5 substantially expands interpretation: similarity measurements are interpreted as reduced parameter and feature movement during fine-tuning; task-dependent gains are linked to representation specificity; and regularization sensitivity is connected to coupling and convexity. It also adds explicit qualifications about theoretical assumptions and a fuller discussion of overhead relative to fine-tuning and scaling to larger models. Existing distribution-mismatch and resource-access limitations remain.

D1.justification: V5 adds detection anchors and parameter-correspondence details, segmentation architecture and preprocessing, new baseline recipes, replacement-head training instructions and similarity-calculation procedures. It adds fine-tuning GPU times and updates the code/weights access pointer from the submission repository to GustavWZ/bissl. However, Section C.6 and Table 14 inconsistently describe the new image resolution as 224px, 224×244 and 244×244.

R1.justification: V5 adds focused references on feature distortion, segmentation and alternative bilevel/Hessian methods, including Kumar et al. (2022), Cordts et al. (2016), Long et al. (2015) and Liu et al. (2024). Several earlier references, including Lorraine et al. (2020), are removed. Section 2's central positioning against existing bilevel SSL and preparatory fine-tuning methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized into an extended-evaluation section and a separate backbone-alignment section. Existing MAE and baseline comparisons move from appendices into the main text, while experimental details are consolidated and reorganized in Appendix B. Citation presentation changes from numbered to author–year.

P2.justification: V5 changes document typography, margins and title/author layout, expands and relocates result tables, and redesigns Table 2 to combine detection and segmentation. It adds cosine-similarity and regularization-sensitivity plots. The t-SNE displays are redrawn, enlarged and reordered with pretraining on the left and BiSSL on the right. The Pets sample-size table and top-5 duration figure disappear.

improvement.justification: V5's data-mixture and zero-head controls better test alternative explanations for BiSSL's gains, while segmentation and sensitivity experiments strengthen evidence about applicability. The explicit significance test and comparison with fine-tuning costs improve transparency. These benefits outweigh the lost Pets sample-size analysis, but new reporting defects limit the gain: Equation (11) misdefines cosine normalization, Section C.6 gives conflicting resolutions, and Table 11 contains an incorrect difference. Overall quality improves modestly, with parts of the new evidence requiring clarification.
